name: BE-DRI
aliases: Behavior Enhances Drug Reduction of Incontinence
question: Does supervised behavioral training added to tolterodine enable women with urge-predominant incontinence to stop medication while maintaining continence improvement?

design.blinding: outcome assessor blinded; participants and interventionists unblinded

arms.label: Tolterodine ER plus supervised behavioral training

design.population: 307 women with urge-predominant urinary incontinence and at least seven weekly leakage episodes were randomized at nine US outpatient centers.
design.description: Two-stage, assessor-blinded, multicenter randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Design Overview, Settings and Participants; Table 1

verdictNote: No demonstrated gain in eight-month drug-free continence success.
takeaway: In BE-DRI, ten weeks of tolterodine ER plus supervised behavioral training versus tolterodine ER alone produced identical estimated eight-month success after drug withdrawal: 41% in each group for drug-free status with at least 70% fewer incontinence episodes.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Kraus SR, Menefee S, et al. "Behavioral Therapy to Enable Women with Urge Incontinence to Discontinue Drug Treatment: A Randomized Trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 2008;149(3):161-169. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-149-3-200808050-00005
reports.followUp: Eight months from randomization, six months after planned drug discontinuation

results.measure: Eight-month life-table success: no urge-incontinence therapy and at least 70% fewer leakage episodes
results.note: Risk difference in percentage points. Observed success was 43/154 versus 41/153; 36 and 34 participants, respectively, lacked final status. Final-analysis alpha was 0.033.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Outcomes after Drug Therapy Discontinuation; Table 2; Methods: Statistical Analysis

results.note: Risk difference in percentage points; 269 women had an evaluable ten-week diary.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Secondary Urinary Symptom Outcomes

results.measure: Eight-month success assuming all missing outcomes were failures
results.note: Sensitivity analysis; risk difference in percentage points.

results.locator: Full text, Results: Patient Global Ratings

results.measure: Eight-month patient rating of better or much better
results.locator: Full text, Results: Patient Global Ratings

harms.label: Participants with adverse events
harms.note: Twelve events occurred in six participants. One combined-arm participant had a serious drug reaction with blurred vision and syncope; small-bowel obstruction occurred in one participant in each arm. There were no deaths.

delivery.label: Tolterodine regimen
delivery.value: Tolterodine ER 4 mg daily for ten weeks, reducible to 2 mg for adverse effects; both arms then discontinued drug, with eight-month follow-up.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Randomization and Interventions; Design Overview

delivery.label: Behavioral training
delivery.value: Four visits over ten weeks with a nurse practitioner, nurse specialist, or physical therapist: pelvic-floor exercise taught with vaginal palpation, urgency suppression, delayed voiding when appropriate, and individualized fluid advice for excessive output.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Randomization and Interventions

delivery.label: Common treatment components
delivery.value: Both arms kept daily bladder diaries and received general fluid-management recommendations during active treatment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Randomization and Interventions

delivery.label: Treatment completion and follow-up
delivery.value: 290/307 attended at least three visits; 208/307 took at least 80% of prescribed drug; eight-month outcome status was known for 237/307.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, opening paragraph and Outcomes after Drug Therapy Discontinuation

reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods: Design Overview; Measurements, Outcomes and Follow-up Procedures
